status: Original Grain remains selected; new rendering studies await user review
userDirection: Explore actual marks, pen-like drawing, tonal grain, light behaviour and colour pop. Original Grain remains preferred over Round 11.

parent.role: Selected whole-image parent / scene and palette control

referenceRoles.role: Sparse pen marks, broad colour fields and coloured-light rendering only

studies.title: Nib
studies.treatment: DRAWING ONLY: introduce clearly visible fine broken ink drawing over the selected Grain painting. Dark petrol/near-black contours vary subtly in weight: confident thin silhouette accents, finer interrupted seams, angular short scratch marks and small directional hatching on rocks/stone, hose ribs, machine curvature and clothing folds. Think scratchy fine technical pen rather than smooth vector outlines. Keep big shapes/calm surfaces; don't trace every object with thick black cartoon borders. Replace some faceted painted micro-detail with legible authored strokes, not extra rust. Maintain original hue/exposure/light and volumetric modeling; no new coloured rim light. Sparse blue/red reference's drawing language is the guide.

studies.title: Etch
studies.treatment: SHADING FROM MARKS: reinterpret smooth/faceted paint tone as visibly drawn shading built from tiny irregular stipple clusters and short close-spaced directional hatch strokes. Density of marks describes cylindrical volume, clothing folds and floor tone; dark regions contain more closely packed dark marks, lit areas more open underlying colour. Keep clean overall silhouettes, existing palette/exposure and same material amount of wear. Substantial etched/stippled illustration finish across world, NOT merely chips, embossed cracked tessellation, uniform grain overlay, regular halftone dots or photorealistic rust. Fine tonal drawing like teal/orange reference, without its teal/orange recolouring. Keep modeled depth with fewer smoother value fields beneath visible marks. Original amber light geometry preserved.

refinement.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Input1 current Etch is EDIT TARGET. Input2 original Grain is composition/palette control. Input3 teal/orange illustration is drawing-technique reference only.
Make ONE targeted correction: radically improve tonal drawing. Current Etch looks like scratched enamel or engraved cracks laid over the unchanged painted render. REDRAW its world as a fine pen-and-stipple coloured illustration, with clearly visible short dark hatch strokes and irregular dense tiny stipple making shadow gradients. Remove scratched crack-like fill from cream casings. Curved casing shadows must visibly be constructed from dense parallel curved pen strokes and dark stipple, thinning toward open cream-lit faces. Floor shadows have flat broad petrol value fields with clusters of short directional strokes at tonal transitions. Clothing folds drawn with hatching. Keep 3D volume but use a smaller number of calm underlying colour fields instead of mottled painted facets. Tonal mark density, NOT damaged materials, creates the form. This change must be obvious at normal scene size, while linework remains fine and varied, not thick cartoon outlines, raised engraved relief or regular dot screens.
Keep exactly the original scene/camera/crop, five people/poses, four trays/bowls, all machinery/architecture/props/decals, petrol/cream/coral/amber colours and original light sites/dark mood. No palette transplant from input3. The actual HUD stays pixel-clean same layout/text/white rules/coral, exempt from drawing/texture. No new objects or wear.

studies.title: Rim
studies.treatment: COLOURED HIGHLIGHT LANGUAGE ONLY: keep original Grain mark-making and scene. Translate broad pale specular highlights into selective fine coloured edge glints: restrained cyan/petrol-blue on cool-facing stone edges, hose rib edges and enamel contour turns, warm amber/coral on existing lamp-facing metal/cream edges. Highlights are narrow graphic strokes that describe form, not neon outlines around everything. Keep cream broad faces cream and petrol shadows dark, local rather than globally teal. Near original mean brightness. No new illumination sources, holograms or blue pools. Some cool edge glints remain richly coloured in darkness; reduce white bleaching of those edge glints. No new black pen outlines, heavier grain, extra wear or bloom. Inspired by reference's coloured edge accents.

studies.title: Chroma
studies.treatment: RICH LIGHT COLOUR ONLY: keep original Grain strokes, texture, shapes and underlying petrol/cream/coral palette. Existing amber lamps/apertures/reflections transfer saturated amber-orange colour onto touched surfaces, retaining rich colour at bright values rather than bleaching to white/cream. Cool shadows retain deep blue-petrol colour rather than drifting brown/neutral. Cream remains cream outside direct narrow warm pools. Less broad pale gloss, stronger colour distinction between existing warm light and cool shadow, with small bright yellow cores in sources only. Preserve same overall dark mood/exposure and light locations, no large extra light areas or new sources. Cast shadow boundaries somewhat clearer, warm surface light still softly rolls into local base colour; no neon outlines, black ink treatment, increased grain or fog. This is coloured-light rendering, not global saturation slider or palette swap.

studies.title: Folio
studies.treatment: SPARSE DRAWN HYBRID based on blue/red reference's render language, while retaining LCL colour family. Combine fine broken dark pen contours, small angular hatching and controlled grain with broad calm opaque colour/shading fields. Group original faceted/mottled microtexture into simpler volume shading; thin ink scratches describe surface/form sparingly rather than rust. Selected narrow coloured highlights: cool muted cyan-blue on shadow-facing edges, warm amber/coral at existing light boundaries. Existing amber working light retains rich colour and less white gloss, subtly softer transitions between broad fields. Dark atmospheric and tactile but unmistakably an authored pen-and-colour illustration at normal scene scale. No thick cartoon contour, uniform cel-shading everywhere, watercolour, raised paint or design/composition changes.

studies.title: Engraved
studies.treatment: DENSE DRAWN HYBRID based on teal/orange reference's render language, while retaining cream/petrol/coral/amber LCL palette. Decisively redraw world shading using fine dark contour seams, densely stippled tonal clusters and tight short directionally hatched strokes following curved machinery/hoses, piers, floor and clothes. Texture participates in creating volume, not enlarged surface pitting. Broad lower-frequency coloured volume remains readable behind the marks. Add selective narrow petrol-cyan edge glints in cool darkness and amber/coral strokes on existing light-facing edges; existing warm light casts richly coloured amber-orange onto local surfaces with little pale bleaching. More assertive contrast and etched illustration character than source while retaining dark pleasant mood and source scene. No extra wear, objects, cyan floodlight, entire cream turned teal, thick all-around outlines, crosshatch mesh, regular halftone or cracks/impasto relief.

Reduce broad naturalistic glossy gradients and mottled paint tessellation; underlying forms use broad grouped opaque cream/petrol value planes with graphic dark shadows. No new scratches/damage: the dark marks are authored pen shading. Existing lit apertures/reflections carry saturated amber-orange with little whitening; cream remains cream outside touched light. Sparse narrow petrol-cyan cool-edge strokes and coral/amber warm-edge strokes add colour pop. Keep dark richness, visibly stronger illustrated tonal contrast and dense printed mark character. Not uniform cel-shading, thick cartoon outlines, stipple everywhere evenly, raised engraving, crackled surface or enamel wear map.
Exact original scene/camera/crop and anchors: five people and poses, four trays/bowls, architecture/props/machinery/physical crests unchanged. No new components, action or composition change.
